newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tanzania to top Anglo Africa exploration.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania to top Anglo Africa exploration.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Friday Tanzania would be the focus of its mining exploration work in Africa in the 1997/98 financial year with a search for promising gold projects there top of its list.
"The country that we are probably going to be most active in in the coming year is Tanzania," Bobby Danchin, chairman of Anglo's new business division, told Reuters in an interview.
Although gold was the key drawcard, the mining giant would keep an eye out for base metal deposits including nickel, he said.
Danchin said Anglo already had a presence in Tanzania both in its own right and in joint ventures with other groups but that it was looking to consolidate and expand this base.

He said mining prospects were becoming harder to come by with many players making small- to medium-size discoveries that might not be sustainable for significant mining on their own. It would become increasingly important to enter into joint ventures and strategic alliances.
"The trick is going to be to try and find a synergy that puts these things together in a cluster," he said.
"I would hope that Anglo is putting out the message that we are open to creative partnerships with governments and other companies."
Danchin said that in the new financial year starting on April 1, Anglo would also continue to be active in the known gold countries of West Africa, notably Mali, Ivory Coast, Ghana and Senegal.

"We recently signed a convention in Senegal which is going to see us quite active there," Danchin said, adding that Anglo also had a big exploration programme scheduled for Zambia, where it would search mainly for copper but also for gold.
"So those are the countries that we see as both prospective and politically inviting," he said.

Danchin said Anglo would in the current financial year spend considerably in excess of $40 million on exploration work in Africa. This figure excluded acquisitions and on site exploration on existing mines such as Anglo's Sadiola Hill mine in Mali.
Although he could not detail expected African exploration expenditure in the 1997/98 he said the search for gold would comprise at least 70 percent of budgeted spending.

Anglo announced last month that the Sadiola Hill mine had completed its first gold pour on December 20. Anglo owns 38 percent of the investment vehicle in control of the mine, Societe d'Exploration des Mines d'Or de Sadiola.
